haiku-low.q1: Only a pending login: no session is created. The server inserts a pending_logins row, sets the p2f cookie, and redirects to the code page.
haiku-low.q2: When setup is confirmed with a valid code, which moves pending_secret into secret. 2FA is on exactly when user_totp.secret is not null.
haiku-low.q3: The recovery code is marked used, enqueue_email notifies the user, then the pending login is deleted and start_session runs. Sign-in does not wait for the email.
haiku-low.q4: Five wrong entries or five minutes elapsed. The pending login is deleted, p2f is cleared, and the user returns to the password page.
haiku-low.q5: Every other session for this user is deleted when setup is confirmed. The current session stays.
haiku-low.q6: No. A code is accepted only if its step is above last_step, set atomically. Drift tolerance is one 30-second step either side.
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: pending_secret becomes secret, last_step is set, old recovery codes are replaced by 10 hashed ones, and other sessions are deleted. Partial-failure outcome is NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q8: In a pending_logins row, referenced by the p2f cookie holding the raw token. Removed on valid code, fifth failure, or expiry, which is rejected on read.
haiku-low.q9: Secret in user_totp.secret (sealed, null until enrolled), replay state in user_totp.last_step, recovery codes as hashes in recovery_codes. 2FA on means secret is not null.
haiku-low.q10: The old secret keeps working until the new one is confirmed, and sign-in ignores pending_secret. If abandoned, nothing changes and the old setup still works.
haiku-low.q11: How the step tells the two apart is NOT STATED. Wrong entries, including already-used recovery codes, each add 1 to failures.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. It is an open question: product has not decided, a support reset is possible, and this plan does not design that path.

sonnet.q1: Only a pending login: a pending_logins row plus the p2f cookie, redirect to the code page. No session is created.
sonnet.q2: Once the setup is confirmed with a valid code (step 2), when pending_secret moves into secret; 2FA is on exactly when user_totp.secret is not null.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is marked used (atomic UPDATE where used_at IS NULL), enqueue_email sends a notice that a recovery code was used and how many remain, the pending login is deleted and start_session is called. Sign-in does not depend on the email; failed sends are retried in the background.
sonnet.q4: 5 wrong entries or 5 minutes (expiry). The pending login is deleted, p2f cleared, and the user goes back to the password step.
sonnet.q5: When setup is confirmed, every other session row for that user is deleted; the current session stays.
sonnet.q6: No; a code is accepted only if its step is greater than last_step, so a replay is rejected. Tolerance is one 30-second step either side of the current step.
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: pending_secret moves into secret and last_step is set; all old recovery codes are deleted and 10 new hashed ones inserted; all other sessions for the user are deleted. If it fails partway, the document does not say explicitly; it only says it is one transaction (and a wrong code changes nothing).
sonnet.q8: In the pending_logins table (token_hash, user_id, expires_at 5 minutes, failures). The browser holds the raw random token in the p2f cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax, max-age 300s); only the sha256 is stored. It is removed on a valid code (row deleted, cookie cleared), on the 5th failure, or on expiry (expired rows are rejected on read; deleting them is just cleanup).
sonnet.q9: All in the user_totp row (one per user): secret (active, sealed via seal()), pending_secret (enrolment status, sealed, awaiting first valid code), last_step (replay protection). Recovery codes are in recovery_codes as sha256 hashes with used_at. 2FA is on exactly when user_totp.secret is not null.
sonnet.q10: The old secret keeps working and is still required at sign-in; sign-in ignores pending_secret. If abandoned, nothing changes: pending_secret is ignored and the old setup still works (a new start overwrites pending_secret).
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED how the server distinguishes them. Wrong entries in general, including already-used recovery codes, are rejected as wrong entries and add 1 to failures, so they count toward the limit of 5.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Product has not decided; it might be a support reset of 2FA, how support would verify identity is undecided, and the plan does not design that path.
